<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments and declarations. Sourcing this file during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will not execute any arbitrary or potentially malicious commands. All variables such as `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, and `sha256sums` are set using literal or predictably constructed strings that reference the project's own upstream GitHub repository. There are no top-level command substitutions, function calls, or eval statements that could lead to code execution or data exfiltration during the sourcing phase.

The `source` and `sha256sums` arrays point to the official GitHub repository of the project, and checksums are provided for all architectures. While checksums are not 'SKIP'ped, that is irrelevant for this gate, as source verification does not occur during `--printsrcinfo`. The presence of architecture-specific sources and sums is normal packaging practice. No remote execution, obfuscation, or suspicious payload handling occurs at parse time.

Thus, parsing this PKGBUILD with `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe, as it involves only data declaration and no active malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No active code execution during parse time.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It lists standard packaging information such as the package name, version, source URLs, checksums, architecture support, and dependencies.

All sources point to legitimate GitHub URLs under the project's official repository (`https://github.com/allisonhere/tide`). The binary assets are fetched from the official releases page, which is expected for a precompiled package. The checksums (sha256sums) are provided for all sources, ensuring integrity verification. There are no network operations, executable scripts, or dynamic downloads in this file.

The package follows standard AUR practices: it provides versioned binaries for multiple architectures, includes appropriate optdepends for optional features, and sets common packaging options (`!strip`, `!debug`). No obfuscated commands, unexpected file operations, or malicious behaviors are present.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard binary package for `tide-bin`, a terminal RSS reader. It retrieves prebuilt, architecture-specific binaries from the project's official GitHub repository (https://github.com/allisonhere/tide) under the `releases/download/v$pkgver/` path, which is consistent with the project's distribution model. The sources are properly checksummed using SHA-256 hashes, and the license file is included from the same release. The package installs only the binary and license to appropriate system locations.

The build process is minimal and safe: it uses `install` to place the prebuilt binary and license file into the package directory. There are no network operations, dynamic downloads, or execution of remote code during packaging. The `options` array disables stripping and debug info, which is reasonable since the binary is already stripped upstream. All dependencies and optional dependencies are clearly declared and appropriate for the application's functionality.

The maintainer metadata and source URLs point to legitimate, expected locations. There is no obfuscated code, suspicious scripting, or unauthorized system modifications. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices for a `-bin` package and poses no evident security risk.
</details>
<evidence>

Standard binary package with verified sources and no malicious behavior</summary>
